'''Marta Lewicka''' (born 23 November 1972) is a [[Poland|Polish]][[United States|-American]] professor of [[mathematics]] at the [[University of Pittsburgh]], specializing in [[mathematical analysis]]. Lewicka has contributed results in the theory of hyperbolic systems of conservation laws, [[fluid dynamics]], [[calculus of variations]], nonlinear elasticity, nonlinear potential theory and [[differential game]]s.

==Career==
Lewicka earned bachelor's and master's degrees in mathematics in 1996 from the [[University of Gdańsk]], and a second engineering bachelor's degree in [[computer science]] in 1998 from [[Częstochowa University of Technology]].<ref name="cv"/> She completed her Ph.D. in 2000 from the [[International School for Advanced Studies]] in [[Trieste]], [[Italy]] under the supervision of [[Alberto Bressan]].<ref name="cv"/><ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=46153}}</ref> After postdoctoral research at the [[Max Planck Institute for Mathematics in the Sciences]] in [[Leipzig]], [[Germany]] and a term as L.E. Dickson Instructor at the [[University of Chicago]], she joined the [[University of Minnesota]] faculty in 2005. She moved in 2010 to [[Rutgers University]], and again in 2011 to the [[University of Pittsburgh]].<ref name="cv">[https://sites.pitt.edu/~lewicka/Lewicka_cv_2022.pdf Curriculum vitae] (2018)</ref>

In 2023-2024 she is the Vice Chair of the Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics Activity Group on Analysis of Partial Differential Equations.<ref>{{cite web |title=SIAM Activity Group on Analysis of Partial Differential Equations|url= https://www.siam.org/membership/activity-groups/detail/analysis-of-partial-differential-equations}}</ref>

==Recognition==
In 2016, she gave an AMS invited address at the AMS/MAA Joint Mathematical Meetings in the area of nonlinear elasticity and geometry of prestrained materials.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://jointmathematicsmeetings.org/meetings/national/jmm2016/2181_invspeakers|title=Joint Mathematics Meetings|website=jointmathematicsmeetings.org|language=en-US|access-date=2019-09-04}}</ref> In 2017, she gave a Howard Rowlee Lecture.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.math.unl.edu/events/rowlee|title=Howard Rowlee Lecture Series {{!}} Department of Mathematics|website=www.math.unl.edu|access-date=2019-09-04}}</ref> In 2017, she received Professor's scientific title, awarded in Poland by the President of the Republic of Poland.<ref>{{citation|title=Ogólnopolski wykaz osób, którym nadano tytuł profesora|url=https://polon.nauka.gov.pl/opi/aa/prof/zestawienie;jsessionid=A2B68BE76C7E92C24DD52D98EA074354.NwsProdD?execution=e1s2}}.</ref> In 2018, she received a Simons Fellowship in Mathematics.<ref>{{citation|title=Simons Fellows in Mathematics| date=19 June 2012 |url=https://www.simonsfoundation.org/grant/simons-fellows-in-mathematics/?tab=awardees}}.</ref>

She was elected a [[Fellow of the American Mathematical Society]] in the Class of 2021,<ref name="AMSfellow">{{cite web |title=2021 Class of Fellows |url=https://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows_by_year.cgi |publisher=American Mathematical Society |accessdate=2 November 2020}}</ref> with citation "For contributions to partial differential equations, calculus of variations, and continuum mechanics." In 2022 she was a fellow of the Lady Davis Foundation<ref>{{cite web |title=Fellows of the Lady Davis Foundation|url= http://ldft.huji.ac.il/fellows}}</ref> and a visiting professor at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem.  She was named as a Fellow of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]], in the 2027 class of fellows, "for sustained leadership and impact in advancing women and girls in mathematics through mentorship, community building, and outreach initiatives".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://awm-math.org/awards/awm-fellows/2027-awm-fellows/|title=2027 Class of AWM Fellows|publisher=Association for Women in Mathematics|access-date=2026-08-21}}</ref>
